focus: parse_text method in CreateStageAutomationMessage and BulkChannelMessageSendJob — verify variable substitution works correctly for subject
seed_note: Used OpenStruct mocks instead of seeded database records due to concurrent agent cleanup races on shared inflow_test database

findings.title: All 7 template variables substitute correctly in subject for both classes
findings.details: Tested {{SenderFullName}}, {{SenderFirstName}}, {{JobTitle}}, {{CandidateFullName}}, {{CandidateFirstName}}, {{CandidateLastName}}, {{OrganizationName}} individually and combined in a single subject string. Both CreateStageAutomationMessage#parse_text and BulkChannelMessageSendJob#parse_text produce identical correct substitutions.

findings.title: nil, empty string, and whitespace-only subject all return '' correctly
findings.details: Both classes return '' for nil, '', and '   ' inputs. The blank? guard on the first line of parse_text handles all three cases correctly.

findings.title: Subjects without variables pass through unchanged
findings.details: Plain text subjects with no {{...}} variables are returned unmodified (aside from html_safe wrapping in CSAM).

findings.title: Unknown variables are left in place unsubstituted
findings.details: Subjects containing {{UnknownVariable}} or {{AnotherOne}} are returned with those placeholders intact, as expected from the gsub-based approach.

findings.title: HTML entities in subject are preserved, not double-escaped
findings.details: Subjects containing &, <script> tags, etc. pass through with variable substitution but no HTML encoding/escaping. This is consistent with the body field behavior.

findings.title: CreateStageAutomationMessage correctly strips NBSP from subject
findings.details: Non-breaking space characters (U+00A0) are replaced with regular spaces by the .gsub(/\u00A0/, ' ') on line 46 of create_stage_automation_message.rb.

findings.title: BulkChannelMessageSendJob does NOT strip NBSP or apply html_safe, unlike CreateStageAutomationMessage
findings.details: CreateStageAutomationMessage#parse_text has .gsub(/\u00A0/, ' ')&.html_safe on line 46 but BulkChannelMessageSendJob#parse_text does not. This means: (1) NBSP characters survive in bulk-sent subject lines but are replaced in automation-sent ones. (2) CSAM returns an html_safe ActiveSupport::SafeBuffer, BulkJob returns a plain String. This may be intentional (automation messages may come from rich-text editors that insert NBSP) or an accidental inconsistency. Same pattern existed for body before subject was added.

findings.title: text.blank? raises ArgumentError on malformed UTF-8 before text.scrub can clean it
findings.details: Both parse_text implementations call `return '' if text.blank?` before `text.scrub`. ActiveSupport's blank? method internally performs a regex match which raises ArgumentError ('invalid byte sequence in UTF-8') on strings with malformed UTF-8 bytes. The scrub call on the next non-blank line never executes. This defeats the stated intent of the scrub call. The same pattern exists in app/models/job_application.rb:549-551. Impact is LOW because browser form input is always valid UTF-8, making malformed bytes in subject (or body) extremely unlikely in production. Fix: change `return '' if text.blank?` to `return '' if text.nil? || text.to_s.scrub.blank?` or call scrub before blank?.

findings.title: html_safe is correctly applied in CreateStageAutomationMessage but not BulkChannelMessageSendJob
findings.details: CreateStageAutomationMessage#parse_text returns html_safe? == true. BulkChannelMessageSendJob#parse_text returns html_safe? == false. Verified via .html_safe? check on return values.
